newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen diving Wednesday on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen diving Wednesday on Iraq.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are likely to take a dive on Wednesday following U.S. attacks on targets in Iraq but securities analysts said they expected the tense situation in Iraq to end soon.
"The market will continue to fall tomorrow (Wednesday) over the mounting tensions," Michael Hung, research manager of Nikko Securities, said on Tuesday.
The U.S. military on Tuesday launched cruise missile strikes against air defense targets in Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds, the Pentagon said.

Taiwan's stock market had closed by the time reports of the U.S. strike on Iraq arrived, but the market's main index already had fallen 1.33 percent or 84.20 points to close at 6,257.97 points on what brokers called investor worries about renewed war in the Gulf.
"What worries people most are the potential rises in domestic oil prices and inflation," said Nikko's Hung.
"But if war breaks out, I think the United States will end it as soon as possible, so the consequences will not be as great as in the first Gulf War," he added.
George Hou, fund manager at Jardine Fleming, agreed that Taiwan's market would take a hit.
"The rising tensions will be a blow to the market," he said. "People had already stepped to the sidelines before the missile strike."
"But the negative impact will be more on the psychological front," he added.
But the United States would try to end any military confrontation as soon as possible in the face of its upcoming presidential election in November, Hou said.
Both Hou and Hung saw initial support at 6,000 points on Taiwan's main stock market index.
